claimCeiling: Retrospective source-backed research memory for conditional routing and checking. Cards do not certify theorem truth, novelty, independent assurance, observed discovery chronology or causal Atlas benefit. Missing conditions remain unknown; source summaries do not replace full proofs or external prior-art review.

cards.title: Replace universal scalar disclosure tests with simultaneous knot completions
cards.summary: For finite scalar quadratic signal tables, including structural zeros, N(q) <= C D(q) for every posterior is equivalent to a common completion z at every distinct source mean t satisfying each supported row loss L_i(z) <= C(x_i-t)^2. C=1 tests the specified disclosure orientation.

actions.label: Build supported row losses
actions.check: Check stochastic rows, supported cell means, x_i=sum_b r_ib v_ib, and one shared completion vector per distinct mean. Do not fill impossible cells with assumed conditional expectations.
actions.stopWhen: Stop theorem application if target scalarity, admissibility, positive prior or supported-data semantics is unverified.

actions.label: Separate orientations
actions.check: Use C=1 for this orientation; reconstruct the reverse conditional table before making a two-sided statement.
actions.stopWhen: Stop a two-sided claim after only one orientation has been checked.

limitations: The cited source is a public summary of an unrefereed analytic candidate, not a proof-assistant certificate.
Finite convex representation is not an implemented general exact solver or polynomial-time bit-complexity theorem.
No extension to arbitrary pairs of partially disclosed signals or other scoring rules.

cards.title: Collapse completions to directed pairs only under full support
cards.summary: Under full rectangular support the completion anchored at x_j is forced to be row v_j. The sharp coefficient is the maximum directed weighted row difference divided by squared mean difference, after separately handling equal-mean incompatibility and the empty-maximum case.

actions.label: Check degeneracies before division
actions.check: Compare equal-mean rows: incompatible conditional means imply infinite coefficient; all equal compatible means give zero.
actions.stopWhen: Stop ratio division when x_i=x_j; use the degeneracy branch.

actions.label: Preserve the normalized objective
actions.check: Only under the stated nondegeneracy use inf G(T)/(V(A)-V(T))=1-R; retain the denominator and limiting-disclosure interpretation.
actions.stopWhen: Stop if the requested result is a minimum absolute gap or general optimal disclosure.

limitations: Full support is needed for this forced-row formula, not for the scalar completion theorem.
An infimum can occur only as a limit; it is not automatically attained by a disclosure.
A target-dependent coefficient is not a channel-only SDPI coefficient.

cards.title: Pairwise-passing sparse rows can fail jointly
cards.summary: In the displayed three-row sparse family, C*=4a^2/(a+b)^2. At (a,b)=(1,1/2), all two-state posterior restrictions pass in one orientation but C*=16/9 and the uniform no-disclosure gap is -1/24. At (1/2,1), C*=4/9 and the normalized margin is positive.

source.locator: ### One sparse family, two different answers

actions.label: Reconstruct the exact family
actions.check: Use channel rows (1/2,1/2,0), (0,1/2,1/2), (1/2,0,1/2) and exactly the source's supported cell means and parameter bounds.
actions.stopWhen: Stop transferring 16/9, 4/9 or -1/24 to another table.

actions.label: Test joint completion
actions.check: Check the simultaneous prescriptions from equal-mean rows rather than separate binary restrictions.
actions.stopWhen: Stop the claim that all pairwise checks certify arbitrary sparse scalar tables.

limitations: This is a specified family and disclosure orientation, not an all-sparse rejection theorem.
The same sparse support has positive and negative cases; zeros alone do not imply failure.
No inference about estimated real-world forecasts.

cards.title: Full support does not rescue pairwise tests for vector targets
cards.summary: The public source records a full-support vector example with six positive directed pairwise margins and a negative three-state residual. A strictly positive four-category probability embedding preserves the failure under quadratic probability scoring.

actions.label: Use the example as a transfer test
actions.check: Inspect the archived vector table and recompute its global residual before treating scalar pairwise sufficiency as a vector theorem.
actions.stopWhen: Stop the unrestricted vector pairwise-sufficiency extension when the exact example is verified.

actions.label: Separate failed proof mechanism from impossibility
actions.check: Record that scalar ordering underlies the interpolation step; search for another finite vector characterization if needed.
actions.stopWhen: Stop short of claiming that no finite vector criterion can exist.

limitations: One-orientation counterexample, not a classification of vector targets.
Four categories are a realization, not a minimality theorem.
The source summary points to vector_exact.py; this card does not reproduce the table or certify it.

cards.title: Distinguish a finite convex formulation from exact certification
cards.summary: The completion theorem supplies an exact real feasibility characterization. Rational failures admit rational violating posteriors, but rational primal completions and rational optimal coefficients are not guaranteed; floating-point boundary feasibility is not an exact certificate.

actions.label: Choose the evidence object
actions.check: For acceptance check all proposed row-loss inequalities exactly; for rejection check the strict posterior residual and admissible disclosure construction.
actions.stopWhen: Stop an exact acceptance claim supported only by numerical solver status or rounded boundary coordinates.

actions.label: Separate model estimation from theorem inputs
actions.check: Record whether support and source means are exact or estimated, especially near coincident means.
actions.stopWhen: Stop treating a plug-in empirical table as a statistical certificate without uncertainty analysis.

limitations: No general exact solver is supplied by the memory card or theorem statement.
Rational failure-witness existence gives no stated polynomial certificate-length bound.
This is a retrospective reusable checking move, not observed discovery chronology or demonstrated time saving.

cards.title: Encode dominating endpoint transversals without changing the graph claim
cards.summary: For a finite simple graph with a maximal matching, choosing one endpoint per matching edge yields Boolean variables. Clauses require domination of unmatched vertices; maximality makes unmatched vertices independent, and each matched vertex is dominated by its edge's chosen endpoint. Satisfying assignments are exactly dominating transversals of that matching.

source.locator: The external bridge is Gupta's Definition 2 and Proposition 6.

actions.label: Recompute the bridge hypotheses
actions.check: Verify the graph and matching directly from edges, then derive clauses from unmatched vertices, retaining tautologies correctly.
actions.stopWhen: Stop if the supplied matching is not maximal or stored metadata disagrees with edges.

actions.label: Check the original representation
actions.check: Reconstruct the selected endpoints and directly test domination of every original vertex.
actions.stopWhen: Stop promoting a SAT assignment that fails graph-level witness checking.

limitations: The bridge does not need cubic regularity, but conclusions about minimum maximal matching may.
It searches transversals of one supplied matching, not all dominating sets.
Implementation-diverse internal checks are not unaffiliated reproduction.

cards.title: An independent-domination counterexample need not refute ordinary domination
cards.summary: The recorded pilot finds 317 endpoint-transversal assignments for the tagged 48-vertex graph and an ordinary dominating set of size 15. With 72 edges and maximum degree 3, the matching lower bound ceil(72/5)=15 and checked matching give gamma <= 15 = gamma_e. The source release separately records independent domination i=16.

source.locator: For the tagged 48-vertex graph the program finds **317** satisfying assignments

actions.label: Bind the witness to its graph
actions.check: Verify the set {0,2,4,7,8,10,13,14,16,18,21,22,24,26,28} against the canonical edges, not merely the order or title.
actions.stopWhen: Stop reuse if input identity or direct domination fails.

actions.label: Keep optimization targets distinct
actions.check: Use the size-15 set as an ordinary-domination upper bound; keep the independent-domination lower bound in its own source scope.
actions.stopWhen: Stop the strengthening route from i>=16 to gamma>=16 on this graph.

limitations: No exact ordinary domination number is established.
The pilot does not recompute the release's independent-domination exclusion certificate.
317 became a regression expectation after execution; it was not the prospective success criterion.
Reduced candidate count is not measured researcher or solver acceleration.

cards.title: Separate budget exhaustion, restricted infeasibility and global impossibility
cards.summary: The workbench requires an exhausted assignment budget to be reported as inconclusive, not UNSAT. Even complete failure to find a transversal of a supplied matching does not exclude an ordinary dominating set: its synthetic 10-vertex control has no such transversal but does have a 3-vertex dominating set.

source.locator: ## Tests that prevent a misleading success

actions.label: Audit search coverage
actions.check: Record tested versus total assignments and whether cancellation or a budget ended the run.
actions.stopWhen: Stop any UNSAT claim when the relevant finite space was not exhausted or otherwise certified.

actions.label: Audit the quantified space
actions.check: Even after exhaustive transversal failure, report only no transversal for this matching; seek a separate global reduction before excluding all dominating sets.
actions.stopWhen: Stop the inference from restricted UNSAT to ordinary-domination impossibility.

limitations: The 50-vertex route control also concerns a supplied matching, not a replay of a global domination lower bound.
Budget exhaustion is missing search evidence, not a mathematical counterexample.
This extraction does not claim that memory would have prevented a past error.

cards.title: A unique numerical answer need not be observation-identified
cards.summary: Under a fixed observation regime, two structural states with identical observable laws cannot be distinguished by more sampling from that unchanged regime. If a target differs across those states, a unique output produced by a prior, constraint or tie-breaker does not identify that target from those observations.

actions.label: Exhibit the semantic counterexample
actions.check: Write the forward observation map and two admitted states with equal observation laws but different target values; keep any selector explicit.
actions.stopWhen: Stop describing the selected target as identified by the focal observations alone.

actions.label: Check the target, not only parameters
actions.check: Ask whether the decision-relevant target remains invariant even when the full parameter does not.
actions.stopWhen: Stop a blanket claim that every target or decision is unidentified merely because the parameter map is noninjective.

limitations: Classical identification principle, not a new theorem claimed by the synthesis.
Exact equivalence must not be replaced silently by a weak or practical ridge.
Nonidentification is not a zero effect and need not preclude a robust decision.

cards.title: Choose a measurement that distinguishes unresolved responses
cards.summary: The public source attributes to Thommen a reaction-network example: two models have identical internal-state path laws at one environmental condition but different stationary responses when that condition changes. The associated benchmark separates a discriminating second condition from condition-specific parameter refitting.

actions.label: Freeze the comparison before adding data
actions.check: Specify which parameters and channel/environment dependence are held fixed across conditions; compare response predictions under those same rules.
actions.stopWhen: Stop claiming discrimination if each model is refitted independently by condition to erase the contrast.

actions.label: Test the new observation direction
actions.check: Check whether the proposed second condition changes predictions along the unresolved direction; include a redundant observation as a negative control.
actions.stopWhen: Stop calling a measurement rank-restoring solely because it adds precision at the original condition.

limitations: Attributed source example, not a new reaction-network theorem derived by this memory.
The public body provides a conceptual counterexample and benchmark pointer; full algebra must be inspected before applying it.
Exact observation-law arguments do not establish identifiability from finite noisy samples.
No empirical effectiveness claim for the Selector Ledger or Atlas.

cards.title: Stress-test literal tensorization on a pure tensor
cards.summary: Under base-2 analytic rank and fixed-order Kronecker powers, a nonzero pure order-three tensor has constant rank a=log_2(4/3). The side-two identity has rank 2a<1, so the literal scalar comparator (2ac)^m tends to zero for 0<c<1 while the pure tensor rank remains a.

source.locator: ## Why every positive power eventually fails

actions.label: Fix conventions before testing
actions.check: Use order three over F_2, the specified pure tensor and side-two identity; derive bias 3/4 and the strict rational comparison 16/9<2.
actions.stopWhen: Stop if the proposed statement instead powers the identity tensor or uses another normalization.

actions.label: Separate analytic proof from finite checks
actions.check: Use the constant left-hand side and decaying comparator for all sufficiently large powers; use finite enumeration only as a diagnostic.
actions.stopWhen: Stop extrapolating an all-power theorem from the checked m=1,2 cases alone.

limitations: Refutes only the stated literal analytic-rank instantiation, not the broader historical problem.
No partition-rank conclusion or claim about the proposer's intent.
No novelty or priority established for the known diagonal mechanism.

cards.title: Compare scaling against the powered identity before pursuing asymptotics
cards.summary: For a diagonal tensor with k active coordinates in side length n, the source gives arank(D^{boxtimes m})/arank(I^{boxtimes m})=(k/n)^m. This isolates why replacing a powered tensor comparator with a repeated scalar rank can change the statement.

actions.label: Audit numerator and denominator scaling
actions.check: Compute both tensor powers on the same diagonal convention and inspect whether the common rank scale cancels.
actions.stopWhen: Stop using the literal scalar-comparator counterexample against this different normalized formulation.

actions.label: Preserve the stopped branch
actions.check: Treat the order-four determinant partition-rank route as incomplete unless its missing asymptotic mechanism is supplied.
actions.stopWhen: Stop claiming a partition-rank solution from the diagonal analytic-rank calculation.

limitations: The ratio is a diagonal comparison, not a general normalized tensorization theorem.
The card is a retrospective design check, not evidence of historical intent or observed discovery order.
A stopped proof route records a missing ingredient, not impossibility of the target.
